tools.name: authenticate
tools.description: Connect to Site Spy with an API key. If the user doesn't have one, ask them to open https://sitespy.app/dashboard to log in and copy their key from the Settings > API tab. The key is held in memory only and is lost when the server restarts — set SITE_SPY_API_KEY to persist it.

tools.name: auth_status
tools.description: Check whether the MCP server is currently authenticated with Site Spy.

tools.name: list_watches
tools.description: List all monitored websites. Returns an object keyed by watch UUID, each with its URL, title, status, and last checked/changed timestamps.

limit.description: Return at most this many watches. Default: all of them.

offset.description: Skip this many watches before returning. Use with limit.

tools.name: create_watch
tools.description: Start monitoring a URL for changes. Returns the UUID of the new watch.

check_hours.description: Hours between checks (default: uses account setting)

fetch_backend.description: How to fetch the page: html_requests (fast, no JS), html_webdriver (browser with JS, for SPAs), or flaresolverr (for Cloudflare-protected pages)

tools.name: get_watch
tools.description: Get full details of a specific watch including its configuration, last check status, and change history summary.

tools.name: update_watch
tools.description: Update a watch's configuration. Use this to pause/resume, change check interval, update title, or modify notification settings.

tools.name: delete_watch
tools.description: Stop monitoring a URL and delete the watch with all its history.

tools.name: get_change_history
tools.description: Get the list of timestamps when changes were detected for a watch. Use these timestamps with get_snapshot or get_diff.

limit.description: Return at most this many entries. Default: all of them.

offset.description: Skip this many entries before returning. Use with limit.

tools.name: get_snapshot
tools.description: Get the page content captured at a specific timestamp. Use get_change_history first to find valid timestamps. Content is capped at 20000 characters by default — raise max_chars if you need more.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters of page content to return. Defaults to 20000.

tools.name: get_diff
tools.description: Compare page content between two timestamps to see exactly what changed. Use get_change_history to find valid timestamps. Output is capped at 20000 characters by default — raise max_chars if you need more.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters of diff output to return. Defaults to 20000.

tools.name: search_watches
tools.description: Search across all watches by URL, title, or content. Returns matching watches.

tools.name: trigger_recheck
tools.description: Force an immediate recheck of every watch. Useful when you need fresh data now rather than waiting for the next scheduled check. Manual rechecks are capped per day by plan.

tools.name: fetch_url
tools.description: Fetch a single known URL through Site Spy. Do NOT use this for discovery — use web_search to find URLs first, then fetch_url on each result. Do NOT fetch google.com / bing.com directly (they always block — wastes the cascade budget). For known static sites prefer fetch_backend: 'html_requests' (≤10s). For SPAs use 'html_webdriver'. For Cloudflare-protected pages use 'flaresolverr'. 'auto' cascades through all three and is capped at 30s total (FETCH_URL_AUTO_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS). On failure, response includes attempts[] and cascade_summary so you can see what was tried. This does not create a watch or save history.

fetch_backend.description: Fetch strategy. Default 'auto' cascades html_requests -> html_webdriver -> flaresolverr with a 30s total cap. Prefer 'html_requests' explicitly for fast static sites.

output.description: Response content format. Defaults to text.

max_content_chars.description: Maximum returned characters for content fields.

timeout.description: Per-backend timeout in seconds (1-120). 'auto' mode also has a separate 30s total wall-clock cap (env FETCH_URL_AUTO_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) that bounds the whole cascade.

wait_seconds.description: Extra browser wait before extracting content.

method.description: HTTP method. Browser fetchers use GET-like navigation.

include_filters.description: Optional selectors used by auto mode to decide if browser rendering is needed.

js.description: JavaScript to execute before extraction when a browser backend is used.

screenshot.description: Return a base64 screenshot when the browser backend captures one.

ignore_status_codes.description: Return content for non-2xx responses instead of failing. Defaults to true.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web via DuckDuckGo HTML and return a list of result URLs with titles and snippets. Use this BEFORE fetch_url when the user asks you to 'search', 'find', 'look up', or otherwise discover content — instead of guessing google.com (which always blocks). Pipeline: web_search(query) -> pick relevant results -> fetch_url(result.url, fetch_backend: 'html_requests') on each. Returns up to 20 results.

limit.description: Max results to return. Default 10, max 20.

debug.description: When true, include a debug_html_excerpt in the response for troubleshooting parsing failures.

tools.name: get_ai_summary
tools.description: Get the AI-generated plain-English summary of a watch's most recent change. Requires a Pro or Business plan. Returns the summary text if available, or a message if no summary exists yet.

tools.name: get_rss_settings
tools.description: Get the current RSS feed settings including whether feeds are enabled and the feed token.

tools.name: generate_rss_token
tools.description: Generate or regenerate an RSS feed token. Use the token to build feed URLs: {server}/rss?token={token} for all watches, {server}/rss/watch/{uuid}?token={token} for a single watch. Regenerating invalidates all existing feed URLs, so any reader already subscribed will stop receiving updates.

tools.name: revoke_rss_token
tools.description: Revoke the RSS feed token, disabling all RSS feed access immediately.

tools.name: get_notifications
tools.description: Get the current notification settings (email, Telegram, web push, etc.).
